title: Check packed weight conversion eligibility before allocating an unpacked projection
applies_when: A post-load weight converter expands a packed projection to test a predicate that may return the input unchanged, such as Humming symmetric INT2–INT8 MoE re-encoding.
lesson: Preserve the scope and representation of the original eligibility check. In Humming offset-binary weights, code zero represents the most negative value and numerical zero is the midpoint. One code zero rejects conversion for the entire projection. Check packed fields directly before unpacking, including fields split across words. Independent per-expert conversion can mix incompatible weight representations. If conversion itself is chunked, decide eligibility globally first and check exact schema, output bytes, unchanged-object returns and the existing zero-point branches. Measure incremental allocator peak and time for both predicate outcomes with the same packed input and runtime.
avoid_when: Verify packing, padding and code semantics for the actual format. The B300 result is for one published Qwen3-30B-A3B INT4 layer-0 W2 projection in Humming 0.1.19. It establishes early-return scratch savings for that method. A synthetic no-zero case kept the same peak. Full-model loading, output quality and inference performance remain unmeasured.

evidence.note: Pinned converter checks the full unpacked tensor and returns the original schema and tensors on a zero code. The guarded B300 original/packed-gate comparison on the complete 128-expert W2 returned the same objects. Additional Torch peak was 1,006,635,520 bytes versus 512 bytes. Reproduction and input hashes are in the Scout humming-int-reencode-chunking record.
The existing vLLM proposal concerns an option to disable re-encoding. A packed eligibility check preserves the original conversion decision and is a distinct dependency-side approach.
